sections.heading: The context
sections.body: Whatarewedoingsef! needed consistent publishing and a clearer understanding of which content formats and topics were connecting with its audience.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.body: I played a key role in building and growing WhatAreWeDoingSef’s digital presence across Facebook, Instagram, Tiktok and Youtube, with content planning, strategy, publishing, scheduling, and day-to-day channel management.

sections.heading: The thinking
sections.body: I paid attention to how different topics performed across platforms, identified stronger audience responses and used those observations to inform content recommendations.

sections.heading: Evidence & outcomes
sections.body:
Facebook: Created and built the page from scratch, growing it to over 1,000 followers within three months.


YouTube: Set up and managed the channel from approximately 3,000 subscribers to over 14,000 in eight months, helping the channel achieve monetisation.


TikTok: Started the account from zero and grew it to over 6,000 followers within six months.


Developed and managed content plans tailored to the brand and its audience.


Coordinated content publishing, scheduling, and consistent posting across platforms.


Managed the overall social media workflow, ensuring content was organised, timely, and aligned with the brand’s communication goals.

sections.heading: What I'd improve next
sections.body: Build a repeatable content testing rhythm, connect each content pillar to a clear audience need and use reporting to guide the next month's creative decisions.

sections.heading: The context

sections.body: Focused on making the user experience clearer and more accessible through structured onboarding, practical video tutorials, responsive communication and ongoing community support.

sections.heading: Evidence & outcomes
sections.body:
300+ users onboarded and guided through the platform.

1,000+ community members supported and managed.

Created tutorial videos to simplify product education.

Supported the technical team with user feedback and issue resolution.

Helped users navigate the app and understand its features.

sections.heading: What I'd improve next
sections.body: Develop a more structured self-service support system, expand the tutorial library and introduce a feedback process that helps the product team identify recurring user challenges.

projects.title: Building a practical starting point for aspiring social media managers
projects.summary: A beginner-focused learning product created to help aspiring social media managers understand the foundations of the role and begin practising with structure.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: I wanted to turn practical social media management knowledge into a clear starting point for people who are curious about the field but do not know where to begin.

sections.heading: What I built
sections.body: A self-paced learning experience with structured video lessons, practical templates and a 90-day implementation phase designed to help learners move from understanding concepts to applying them.

sections.heading: The experience behind it
sections.body: This project brings together my experience as a social media practitioner, content strategist and educator. It also demonstrates curriculum planning, information design, audience understanding and learner experience.

sections.heading: Evidence to add
sections.body: Add approved screenshots of the programme, lesson previews, template samples, learner feedback and any verified enrolment or completion figures when available.

sections.heading: Why it belongs in my portfolio
sections.body: It shows that I do not only execute social media work for brands. I can also develop a learning product, organise information and create practical resources for a defined audience.

projects.note: Founder-created programme. Add actual product visuals and learner feedback only when approved and available. Do not imply learner outcomes or sales figures without evidence.

projects.title: A thoughtful support journey from first message to resolution
projects.summary: A sample customer-support workflow designed to make responses more consistent while keeping the experience personal and useful.

sections.heading: The scenario
sections.body: A customer has paid for a digital service but cannot access their account. They have already contacted the business once and are frustrated.

sections.heading: The response principles
sections.body: Acknowledge the inconvenience, confirm the relevant details safely, explain the next step and set a realistic expectation for follow-up.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body: Receive and categorise the enquiry, verify the issue without requesting sensitive credentials, resolve or escalate, confirm the outcome and record the case.

sections.heading: Sample assets
sections.body: Add an anonymised ticket example, response templates, escalation matrix, FAQ and a simple support tracker.

sections.heading: Success measures
sections.body: Track first response time, resolution time, reopened tickets, customer satisfaction and recurring issue themes.

projects.note: Self-initiated concept project. The workflow is illustrative and should be adapted to each company's policies and tools.
